note: CANDIDATE declarations for the aircraft successor profile, each evaluated separately in shadow before any decision (PROFILE_REPAIR_PROPOSAL.md). R-BAD is NOT a proposal: it is the deliberately wrong over-connection used to show what an unacceptable repair looks like.

R1.justification: v1.1 defines COARSE_NAVIGATION as requiring the gps source; the profile declares gps rides gnss_serial. A position that cannot arrive cannot serve the function.

R2.justification: the v2 function table declares COMPUTE a SUPPORTING domain of COARSE_NAVIGATION (degrade, not remove), but no compute component names it, so the declaration is dead. On a PX4-class multirotor every position output is the estimator's output.
R2.source: engineering/v2/FUNCTION_DEPENDENCY_SPEC.md section 6; csia/v2/profiles/aircraft.py COARSE_NAVIGATION acceptable_degradation; PX4 EKF2 architecture (V0)

R3.justification: TIMING is likewise a declared SUPPORTING domain of COARSE_NAVIGATION with no timing component naming it. nav_solution is the channel that carries the position (aircraft.py comment on nav_solution).

R4.justification: G-3: every v1.1 GNSS-requiring function (required_sources gps) depends on the link gps rides; the link names only SENSING.

R5.justification: G-2: the estimator fuses GNSS; the GNSS measurement reaches it over gnss_serial. The profile declares only cpu and imu0 as inputs, so OUTPUT_MISSING can never test 'the estimator's input link is down'.
R5.source: csia/v2/profiles/aircraft.py ProcessSpec state_estimator and ChannelSpec nav_solution comment; PX4 EKF2 input set (V0)

R6.justification: the other estimator inputs. Physically real; no current predicate or relation consumes them for the estimator.

R-BAD.justification: NOT A PROPOSAL. The ESC CAN bus carries motor telemetry and commands only; it serves no navigation function. Used to demonstrate an over-connection that restores frozen v2's false symptom.
